scope: the whole soldier: proportions, silhouette, placement, layering, the hold, and the first materials (values, colours, wear) against the reference; ignore fine surface detail

merged.text: The trousers are tights: crotch and seat sculpted through the cloth, thighs skin-tight, then a stiff baggy tube below the knee. Real G3-style trousers have even ease and a gusseted crotch.
also: The trousers cling at the crotch and seat like leggings. Combat trousers hang loose there.
The trousers are skin-tight at the crotch and seat like leggings; the reference's combat trousers hang loose with folds above the knee.
Trousers are skin-tight through hips, crotch, thighs and seat: the crotch bulge and buttock forms show through, then the leg flares into a stiff baggy tube below the knee.
Trousers are skin-tight from waist to knee, showing crotch and buttocks like leggings, then baggy below; real G3-class trousers hang loose from the hips.
Trousers are skin-tight over crotch, thighs and seat (anatomical bulge in front, buttock seam at the back), then baggy below the knee; they read as leggings.
fixes: Crye G3-class cut: roomy seat and thighs, gusseted crotch, folds where the fabric hangs.
Crye G3-class trousers hang with 40-60 mm ease at the thigh, a gusseted crotch and a straight seat; volume is continuous from hip to cuff.
G3-class trousers hang from the hips with a crotch gusset, pocket volume and folds at the hip crease, loose over the thigh.

merged.text: The right pauldron sticks out like a fin off the shoulder instead of capping it. It breaks the silhouette and looks unattached.
also: The right pauldron is a flat plate standing off the top of the shoulder like a fin, with a second flat card below it; it neither wraps the deltoid nor rests on it.
The right pauldron is a flat card tilted off the shoulder; real shoulder guards are moulded shells that cup the deltoid. The pauldrons also make the shoulder outline smaller than drawn.
The right pauldron is a flat thin card tilted off the shoulder, its top edge standing clear of the deltoid instead of a domed shell following it.
Pauldrons are paper-thin flat cards tilted off the deltoids, with no molded curvature or thickness.
The soldier's right pauldron is a paper-thin flat card tilted off the deltoid with a gap beneath, no thickness and no curvature following the shoulder.
fixes: A real shoulder guard is a curved cap shaped to the deltoid, strapped flush, with the upper-arm plate hinged below it.
A shoulder guard is a moulded shell of 3-5 mm wall that cups the deltoid and is strapped down to it.
A molded shell several mm thick that wraps the deltoid and is strapped down onto the sleeve.

merged.text: The knee pads are soft black pillows; the reference's are faceted hard caps with tan frames.
also: The knee pads are rounded black pillows with tan flecks; the reference's pads are angular hexagonal hard caps with a raised tan/olive frame round a dark faceted plate.
Knee pads are pillow boxes with inverted values (black with tan blotches). The reference shows tan hard caps in dark frames.
Knee pads are rounded pillow boxes in black with tan blotches, value inverted from the reference's tan hard caps in a dark frame, with no cap-and-sleeve construction.
Knee pads are pillowy boxes with leopard-spot decal blotches, missing the hard faceted cap and rim.
Knee pads are pillowy rounded boxes with even leopard-spot tan blotches that read as a camo decal, not scuffing; no hard cap edge.
fixes: AirFlex-class pad: faceted hard cap with a raised rim, tan/olive frame and dark centre, buckled strap at the side.
AirFlex-class pads: a contoured hard cap over a thinner foam body, cap edges framed, strap slots at the sides.
AirFlex class: a hard faceted cap with a defined rim over a fabric sleeve, scuffs on the most prominent face and dust in creases.

merged.text: Boots read as sneakers: smooth wrapped uppers, thin wedge soles, no toe cap, laces only at the ankle. A Zephyr-class boot laces from the toe box and has a deep lugged sole.
also: The boots read as smooth galoshes, with no toe cap, panels or stitching, in flat grey.

The right boot reads as a smooth galosh: a plain upper with no toe cap or panels above a high flat rand; the reference boot has a scuffed rubber toe cap, stitched leather panels and a chunky lugged sole.
The right boot reads as a sneaker bootie: one smooth wrapped upper, no toe cap or rand, a thin wedge sole, and laces only on the ankle shaft.
The soldier's right boot is a smooth seamless shell with no toe cap or forefoot lacing; it reads as a galosh, not a Zephyr-class boot.
The soldier's right boot vamp is a seamless smooth shell with one sweep line, no toe cap and no lacing toward the toe; it reads as a galosh or sneaker.
fixes: Zephyr-class boot: separate toe bumper, suede/nylon panels with stitch lines, distinct midsole and lug outsole.
Zephyr-class boots lace from the toe box to the collar, with suede and textile panels, a rubber toe rand and a 30-40 mm lugged sole.
Zephyr class: suede and textile panels with seams, a rubber toe bumper, eyelets running down to the forefoot, creases at the flex point.

merged.text: A thin disc floats edge-on off the left elbow where the reference has an elbow pad.
also: The left elbow pad is a thin disc where the reference has a thick cap.
The left elbow pad is a thin disc on the point of the elbow; the reference shows a thick hard elbow cap that stands well proud of the sleeve.
A thin disc stands edge-on off the outer left elbow, floating clear of the sleeve, instead of an elbow pad wrapping the joint.
Elbow pads seen edge-on are thin bright metal slivers standing off the elbows.
The elbow pad seen edge-on is a paper-thin bright metal disc standing off the elbow; the soldier's right elbow shows the same sliver.
fixes: A moulded elbow cup about 20 mm thick over the olecranon, strapped round the arm.
An elbow pad is a curved cap of 15-25 mm foam with a hard shell, strapped around the joint.
An elbow pad is a padded shell about 15 mm thick wrapping the joint, matte, strapped over the sleeve.

merged.text: The armour reads as black metal with white paint chips everywhere; the reference's plates are worn tan/olive with blue-grey steel faces. This one colour choice changes the whole figure's identity.
also: Pauldrons, arm bands and forearm guards are near-black with a white salt-and-pepper speckle, like chipped black paint; the reference's armour is worn tan/olive with blue-grey steel faces and soft brown wear.
Armour material reads as painted steel: dark grey with bright white chips. The reference's plates are tan-olive polymer that wears paler at the edges.
Pauldron, arm bands and forearm guard render as dark grey painted metal with bright white paint chips; the reference armour is tan-olive polymer with worn edges.
fixes: Base the plates on the reference's olive-tan polymer with blue-grey steel face plates; wear as edge abrasion and brown grime, not white flecks.
Polymer armour scuffs to a paler matte of its own colour along edges, not bright metal under paint; base value should be mid tan-grey.

merged.text: The hair is a dark rubber cap with a cut-out hairline and shards on the crown; with the declared default skin, the head reads as a game NPC at a glance.
also: Hair is a hard-edged cap with spiky tufts on the crown; it gives the head away at native size even with the declared default skin.
Hair is a solid cap with a hard edge across the forehead and temples and spiky polygon tufts on the crown; it reads as a helmet or a painted skull.
Hair is a smooth dark shell with a hard cut-out hairline and jagged triangular shards on the crown; no strands, no fade at the temples, it reads as a rubber cap.
fixes: Short hair thins at the hairline into skin and stands as fine strands, darker at the roots.
A short crew cut: strand cards or curves, density fading to stubble at temples and nape, a soft broken hairline.

merged.text: The carrier is a plain pale khaki slab. The reference's carrier, the centrepiece, is olive-brown, busy and bulky, with a placard and tall flapped pouches.
also: The carrier front is a plain flat light grey-khaki slab with three short open shingles; the reference is olive-brown with a laser-cut placard, admin panel and tall flapped pouches.
The carrier front is a flat khaki slab with dead-straight edges and box pouches, no PALS, binding or stitching; the reference carrier is busy, bulky webbing.
The carrier front is a flat khaki slab with dead-straight edges and soft rounded corners; the mag pouches are plain boxes; no PALS, binding, stitching or fabric creasing.
fixes: Olive-brown worn Cordura, a raised placard with its panel and three tall flapped magazine pouches reaching toward the belt.
JPC-class front: MOLLE rows or laser-cut slots, bound edges, stitched pouches with flaps and bungee, fabric slack and creases.

merged.text: Gloves are smooth rubber with sausage fingers and mannequin poses; no knuckle guards, seams or palm patches.
also: Gloves are smooth rubber with thick, rounded fingers and no knuckle guards.
Gloves are smooth rubber with thick sausage fingers and no knuckle or finger protection.
Gloves are smooth rubber with sausage fingers, no knuckle guards, seams or palm patches, posed stiffly like mannequin hands.
fixes: M-Pact-class gloves have TPR knuckle and finger guards, a seamed back and a palm patch.
M-Pact class: TPR knuckle and finger guards, stitched panels, synthetic leather palm, creasing at every knuckle.

merged.text: A rear belt pouch hangs off the back of the hip with its flap jutting out; it is not carried by the belt.
also: A rear belt pouch hangs well behind the hip with its flap jutting outward, not seated against the belt or the body.
A pouch on the back of the belt stands off the hip with a visible gap, floating rather than hanging against the seat.
A tall pouch on the back of the belt stands away from the hip at an angle with a clear gap, not resting on the body.
fixes: A belt-mounted pouch rides flush on the belt's MOLLE, its back against the belt with no gap.
It hangs from the belt and lies against the seat, following its curve.

merged.text: The shirt and sleeves are painted on: no ease anywhere, upper arms are smooth cylinders and the back view shows shoulder blades. The reference's bulk comes from padded sleeves.
also: Combat shirt body and sleeves are painted onto the skin: no fabric ease at shoulders, elbows or upper arms; arms read as smooth tubes and the shoulder blades show in the back view.
fixes: A combat shirt's sleeves carry padding and 20-30 mm ease, with fold mass at the elbow crook and armpit.

merged.text: Every hard plate carries the same uniform white speckle; it reads as procedural salt noise. Real wear sits on edges and corners, low contrast, with dirt in the recesses.
also: The white speckle wear on pauldron, arm bands and forearm guards is one high-contrast noise at one scale everywhere, reading as procedural salt rather than wear.
fixes: Wear concentrated on edges and raised corners, low contrast, scuffed through to substrate, with dirt in recesses and flat areas left mostly intact.

merged.text: [D4] The arm armour is in the wrong places and sizes: the left upper-arm plate is short, and the right forearm guard sits at the elbow with the forearm bare under a long glove.
also: On the left arm the reference's long upper-arm plate, running from the shoulder cap almost to the elbow, is replaced by a short square plate and a strap band; the outer upper arm shows bare sleeve.
fixes: One tall curved plate on the outer upper arm from under the shoulder cap to about 60 mm above the elbow, held by two straps.

merged.text: The left hand rests on the handguard instead of gripping it, so the hold looks posed rather than carried.
also: The left hand lies on top of the handguard with its fingers hanging down the far side; it does not close round the handguard as the reference's supporting hand does.
fixes: Palm under and beside the handguard, fingers curled up over its far side, thumb along the near side.

merged.text: Carrier shoulder straps kink up off the trapezius as flat planes with daylight under them; under a plate's weight real straps lie flat and bear on the shoulder.
also: Carrier shoulder strap panels kink upward as flat planes and stand off the trapezius with a visible gap, on both shoulders.
fixes: JPC-class shoulder straps are padded webbing lying on the trapezius under tension from the plate weight.

merged.text: The trousers are grey-washed and get lighter toward the cuffs; the reference's are dark charcoal with brown mud.
also: The trousers read mid-grey with pale camo blotches and grow lighter toward the cuffs; the reference's trousers are dark charcoal-brown with muddy tan patches.
fixes: Darker charcoal base with brown-tan mud staining concentrated at the knees and shins, no pale grey wash.

merged.text: Sleeves and shirt are seamless smooth tubes with no folds at elbow or shoulder and no fabric texture; it reads as a wetsuit.
also: The sleeve is a seamless smooth tube with no folds at the elbow bend, no seams and no fabric texture; the shirt reads as a wetsuit.
fixes: Combat shirt sleeves bunch and crease at the elbow inside, show seams and a matte knit texture.

merged.text: The gloves are smooth rubber with long gauntlets; the reference's have knuckle armour and short cuffs.
also: The gloves are smooth rubbery mitts with sausage fingers and long gauntlet cuffs; the reference's gloves are M-Pact-class with knuckle armour, padded panels and a short cuff.
fixes: Short-cuff mechanic-style glove with a moulded knuckle guard, finger panels and a wrist strap.

merged.text: The trouser weave is coarse burlap at a far too large scale, visible in the full view, under soft cloud-noise camo.
also: The trouser fabric shows a coarse burlap weave far too large for ripstop, visible even in the full view, under soft cloud-noise camo with no defined edges.
fixes: A fine ripstop grid near invisible at this distance; camo and dirt with defined shapes, dirt heavier at knees and cuffs.

merged.text: The hair is a hard cap with a jagged top. With the declared parametric face it makes him read as a younger, rounder, different man and weakens every judgement of the whole figure.
also: The hair is a solid dark cap with a jagged top edge and a hard painted hairline; the reference has short textured mid-brown hair with volume swept up on top and faded sides.
fixes: Strand or card hair, longer and lifted on top, short taper at the sides, mid-brown.

merged.text: Trouser hems stack in regular accordion rings, identical on both legs, instead of irregular blousing over the boots.
also: Above both boots the trousers stack in regular horizontal rings like an accordion, the same on both legs.
fixes: Real stacking over a boot top is irregular, with diagonal folds and one or two deep breaks, best from a cloth simulation.

merged.text: The right thigh mag pouches are oversized boxes, and their black plastic is too clean against the reference's worn kit.
also: The right thigh rig is two oversized flat black boxes with slots, wider and squarer than the reference's slimmer worn holster and magazine pouches.
fixes: Narrower kydex-style mag carriers sized to a STANAG magazine, with the reference's worn tan/olive edge wear.

merged.text: The shoulders are square and high with no trapezius slope, which reads mannequin-like next to the reference's sloped shoulders.
also: The shoulder line is square and high, nearly level from neck to deltoid; the reference's shoulders slope down from a visible trapezius.
fixes: Lower and round the shoulder tops so the line falls from the neck to the deltoid.

merged.text: The left shoulder emblem is a star; the reference's is a crossed-blade X on a shield.
also: The emblem on the left pauldron is a pale star on a grey panel; the reference shows a crossed-blade X mark on a dark blue-grey shield-shaped panel.
fixes: Reproduce the reference's X/crossed-blade mark and the shield outline and colour of its panel.

merged.text: The right forearm guard is a short cuff sitting at the elbow; the forearm below is covered by a long smooth glove gauntlet, where the reference has a segmented guard from below the elbow to the wrist.
fixes: Move the guard down to span mid-forearm to wrist, segmented plates over a strap base, with the glove cuff ending under it.

merged.text: The left hand clamps the handguard from above with fingers dangling; it does not look as though it is bearing the carbine's weight.
also: Left hand clamps the handguard from above with the thumb over the rail and fingers hanging, the palm not seated against the handguard.
fixes: A support hand cups the handguard from beneath or wraps it, palm in contact, fingers closed around it.

merged.text: The carbine is one flat dark grey, missing the reference's tan accents and edge wear.
also: The carbine is a flat even dark grey with no wear on the edges and no tan accents; the reference's carbine is gunmetal with tan anodised parts and worn edges.
fixes: Black/gunmetal anodised finish with lighter worn edges and the reference's tan accents on the stock and receiver.

merged.text: The handguard top renders as black-and-white zebra stripes like hazard tape.
also: The top of the handguard renders as black-and-white zebra stripes, like hazard tape, from the rail slots or an aliased texture.
fixes: Rail teeth read as dark anodised ridges with small soft highlights, never high-contrast bands.

merged.text: [D16] Small pieces stand off what holds them: a strap pad corner beside the neck, and an L-shaped item jutting from the rear belt.
also: The pad at the top of the right shoulder strap pokes up beside the neck as a flat card corner instead of lying over the shoulder.
fixes: Strap pads drape over the trapezius and follow it down front and back.

merged.text: The carrier's shoulder pads are thin flat cards with stepped edges and a black void beneath.
also: The carrier's shoulder pad is a thin flat card with stepped edges and a black void beneath it.
fixes: A padded shoulder strap with thickness and bound edges, resting on the shoulder.

merged.text: Stray triangular spikes poke up from the top of the soldier's right shoulder.
also: Small stray triangular spikes poke up from the top of the soldier's right shoulder, like torn cloth or stray hair geometry.
fixes: Remove the stray faces; the shoulder line is a clean fabric curve under the carrier strap.

merged.text: An L-shaped item on the rear right of the belt projects well behind the hip and does not appear to rest on the belt.
fixes: Seat the item flat against the belt with its loop round the belt.

merged.text: Overall mass is far below the reference: a lean young body in skin-tight cloth with thin flat plates, against a man bulked by layered kit. Even with correct placement it reads as a costume.
Mass overall: thin carrier, thin band-like arm armour, slim thighs and smooth sleeves make the man read lighter, younger and cleaner than the reference's loaded soldier.
Trouser lower legs are much lighter (pale grey) than the reference's charcoal with tan dirt; the leg value jumps from dark at the thigh to near-white at the cuff.
The battle belt is a narrow flat strap; a belt carrying thigh rigs and pouches is about 50 mm wide and padded, and should read as a band at the waist.
Posture is more upright than the reference, with the chin lifted, so the man looks up and out rather than settled back on his heels.
The carbine is uniform matte grey with no anodising variation, edge wear or dust; next to the worn kit it reads as an untextured asset.
The shirt sleeves are perfectly smooth tubes with no seams or folds, so the arms read inflated rather than clothed.
The firing hand lies on the receiver with a stiff straight index and no visible wrap around the pistol grip, so the hold reads placed, not gripped.
Carrier colour is a desaturated khaki-grey with a flat plate face and no webbing rows; the reference's carrier is olive-coyote with PALS and visible pouch bulk.
Trouser cuffs stop short above the boot collar instead of breaking over the boot tops as the reference shows.
